prerequisites: Basic understanding of mechanical and thermal processes

learning_outcomes.text: Students expand their knowledge of the basic operations of EUV-T to specific processes of drinking water, wastewater, and exhaust air treatment, as well as soil decontamination.
Students can describe and design the processes and plant technology for environmental engineering applications in detail. They can place the procedures in the context of legal regulations.
Students can select and comparatively evaluate suitable processes.
Students develop solutions for concrete environmental engineering problems. They evaluate the results of experimental laboratory tests in the context of specialized literature.
Students can compare different environmental technology solutions, develop proposed solutions in teamwork, and present them in a structured manner.
Students link various skills learned during their studies, can assess and reflect on their own competencies.

syllabus_topics: Limit values and requirements for water, air, and soil
assessment_rules: The choice of examination type (written or oral) is at the discretion of the examiner and will be communicated to students at the beginning of the semester. The graded assessment is either a 2-hour written exam or an oral examination. An ungraded experimental work consisting of 2-4 experiments is also required.
